newsitem.title: UK: Argentina plans 500 bln lire 10-year bond -dealers.
newsitem.headline: Argentina plans 500 bln lire 10-year bond -dealers.

text.p: Argentina plans to launch a 500 billion lire 10-year bond as early as next week, syndicate managers said on Tuesday.
"Argentina has said it will issue a lira deal, and this is likely to be a 500 billion lire 10-year issue," said a new issues trader at a European bank.
"The bond is expected to surface next week," he said.
Chase was tipped as lead manager for the transaction, but officials there declined to comment.
Spread talk on the Argentina bond was between 265-275 basis points over swaps, traders said.
Earlier this month, Argentina's finance secretary Pablo Guidotti said Argentina would launch a lira bond this year.
He said it was also considering issuing $1.5-$2.0 billion in bonds to finance 1997 spending needs.
Other funding plans included a $400-$500 million bond to finance public sector dismissals and job retraining in 1996 and a 500 billion yen bond in the first quarter of 1997.
Argentine oil company YPF tapped the Eurolira sector on Tuesday with a 300 billion lire five-year bond via joint lead managers Chase and Banca Commerciale Italiano.
